newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Sofia police motorcyclists target crime - by day.
newsitem.headline: Sofia police motorcyclists target crime - by day.

text.p: Bulgaria has set up a special police motorcycle squad to crack down on car theft and armed robbery -- but only during the day, because streets in the capital Sofia are so bad that crime fighters on two wheels would risk their lives at night.

Sofia police chief Emil Tanev said on Tuesday that the rapid-response squad, called Sigma, would consist of 100 police officers equipped with Scorpion automatic rifles, bulletproof jackets and radios, 60 Czech MZ motorcycles and 10 German BMWs.

"At this stage the squad will be operating only during the day as we cannot afford to risk the lives of our people at night because riding a motorcycle in Sofia's bumpy streets in the dark is very dangerous," Tanev told a news conference.
The new government, which took office in May, has pledged to rein in organised crime and corruption flourishing since the fall of Bulgaria's longtime communist regime in 1989.
